title: The Future of Research Infrastructure
lines: The Future of Research Infrastructure asks what must persist when research models keep changing.
Its answer centers on a scientific project state that connects claims, evidence, and decisions.
The book follows how proposed work becomes executed, evaluated, and accepted knowledge.
Documents and agents become participants around that shared record, rather than its only memory.
Readers can examine a research architecture designed for continuity, accountability, and replaceable tools.

title: What the project actually knows
lines: Documents, notebooks, conversations, and agents can disagree about the current state of one project.
The proposed infrastructure gives questions, evidence, claims, and decisions persistent identities and relationships.
Versions make changes visible rather than silently replacing the account of earlier work.
Models and interfaces can change while the project's evidential continuity remains inspectable.
This is the architectural difference the book develops beyond a larger collection of research tools.

title: A result must cross several stages
chapter: A result must cross several stages
lines: A proposed analysis is not yet an executed analysis or an accepted scientific result.
The book separates proposal, execution, evaluation, and commitment within a research transaction.
Different tools and people retain different responsibilities and guarantees.
Human authority remains visible at consequential transitions instead of disappearing inside an autonomous workflow.
The design aims to preserve scientific meaning as more work becomes machine assisted.

title: Read one complete research episode
lines: The implementation discussion recommends a narrow scientific episode supported from beginning to end.
A pilot would need to demonstrate value before adding more speculative capabilities.
The book also asks whether its architecture improves on simpler existing arrangements.
Read the opening architecture alongside the chapters explaining each responsibility it introduces.
